Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

statomatic 1.0.0

A rebuild of statomatic. The statistical approach is unchanged: each row is sorted by the normality of its residuals and the equality of its group variances, and then analyzed with the matching tests. For one-factor designs, the results are the same as in earlier versions (tested against saved results of the previous version). This release has breaking changes.

Breaking changes

  • multigroup_main() and twogroup_main() take the sample table and the names of its factor columns: multigroup_main(x, sample_info, factors = c("condition", "sex")). This replaces the var1, var2 and var3 arguments.
  • Samples are matched to the columns of x by name, through a sample ID column of sample_info (found automatically), its row names, or sample_col. The analysis stops with an error if samples can’t be matched, instead of assuming that the order is the same.
  • For two and three factors, the pairwise tests (Tukey, Dunnett T3, Dunn), the Welch and Kruskal-Wallis tests and the fold changes use the combinations of all factors as groups (e.g. Female_KO), built automatically. Previously they used one factor (var3, by default the first factor).
  • ANOVA uses Type II sums of squares (car::Anova()), so results don’t depend on the order of the factors. With two or more factors and unequal group sizes, the main-effect p-values differ from earlier versions (Type I).
  • Result columns are named pvalue_*, padj_* and log2FoldChange_* (previously Pval_* and Padj_*). In each result table, the columns of each comparison are next to each other: pvalue, padj, log2FoldChange.
  • padj = TRUE is the default for all functions (previously FALSE).
  • The test functions (run_ttest(), run_tukey(), …) still take the data and the group labels, but the data argument is now called x (previously my_data), and all of them have padj and include_test_name arguments. test_norm() and run_anova() take the factors as a vector (one factor) or a data.frame (several factors) instead of var1 and var2.
  • test_norm() returns a named list (ne, nu, nn, tests).
  • fold_change() no longer has a FUN argument.

Removed

  • The S4 interface: make_sds(), sds_analyze(), the sds_*() methods and the get_*() accessors. Use multigroup_main() and twogroup_main() directly. The SummarizedExperiment dependency is removed with it.
  • combine_fc_pvals(), chop() and takeN().
  • Adunn.test(), AdunnettT3Test() and p.adjustment.methods, modified copies of dunn.test::dunn.test() and PMCMRplus::dunnettT3Test(). Statomatic now has its own implementations of Dunn’s test and Dunnett’s T3 test, which give the same results as the copies (current dunn.test versions give different p-values than the 1.3.6 copy). The PMCMRplus dependency is removed.
  • The write_files and file_names arguments of the main functions. Use write.csv() on the results.

New features

  • test_norm() and the main functions return a tests table with each row’s Shapiro-Wilk and Levene p-values and the set it was sorted into.
  • shapiro_threshold and levene_threshold set the significance levels used to sort rows (both 0.05 by default).
  • log_input = TRUE in fold_change() and the main functions, for data that is already log-transformed: fold changes are then differences of group means.
  • run_anova() and test_norm() support any number of factors (the main functions support up to three).
  • The design is checked before the analysis: missing samples, missing values, factors that are not fully crossed, groups with fewer than 2 samples, and more than 3 factors give clear errors.
  • verbose = TRUE prints progress messages in the main functions.
  • A set without rows gives a 0-row results table with the usual columns.

Other changes

  • Missing values are dropped per row in the tests and ignored in group means.
  • Comparison names (A_vs_B) and their order are the same in every locale.
  • Groups with identical constant values in Dunnett’s T3 test give p = 1 instead of an error, as in earlier versions.
  • From R 4.6.0, wilcox.test() computes exact p-values for data with ties, so Wilcoxon p-values for tied data differ between R versions.
